function: p. 6-8: DDPG learns RIS passive phase-shift beamforming and MEC computing allocation jointly with DDQN-learned service caching and task offloading, to minimize total task completion delay.
system: p. 4-5, 9: AP and ten devices with scalar channel coefficients (single antenna implied), passive reflecting RIS with 30 elements, 1 MHz bandwidth; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 6-8: hybrid deep reinforcement learning, DDQN for discrete caching/offloading plus DDPG for continuous computing allocation and RIS phases; agent interacts with simulated environment, experience replay.
data_channel: p. 9: simulated Rician channels with path loss (Eq. 30, reference -30 dB, exponents 2.2/2.2/3.7) in a 50 m x 50 m area; no dataset or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 9-11: trained and evaluated in one simulated environment; parameters swept (CPU cycles, caching, computing capability, task size, RIS elements, DT deviation); no test on unseen conditions stated.
baselines: p. 9-10: ablations without RIS and with random RIS phase; random caching/offloading (RSCCO); all-cloud (CC); learned DDPG scheme of [42] on the same problem.
metrics: p. 10-11: total task completion delay (s) and reward versus training episodes; average delay reduction (56.8%, 13.8%, 11.9%, 16.2% over four baselines, Fig. 5).
complexity: p. 9: order of training complexity O(I Tmax tmax (Z G0 + sum of layer-size products)) over DDQN, actor and critic layers; no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime.
openness: none: p. 9 states only TensorFlow 2.12.0 and Python 3.10; no code or data link.
q1_support: p. 9: "the channels are modeled as [38]" - custom Rician plus path-loss model (Eq. 30, Table III); no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "different CPU cycles for processing one bit of task data" - only sweeps of environment parameters (also caching, computing, task size, RIS elements, DT deviation); no unseen scenario, band or dataset, and no transfer or fine-tuning, is stated.
q3_support: p. 10: "DDPG Scheme in [42]: The optimization problem in (17) is addressed by the DDPG algorithm" (learned); non-learned: random RIS phase, RSCCO and CC; all compared on total task completion delay in Figs. 4-8.
q4_support: p. 8: "We analyze the complexity of our HDRL algorithm"; p. 9 gives the order O(I Tmax tmax (...)) of its training as a function of layer sizes.
q5_support: p. 9: "we train the proposed learning framework using TensorFlow" - channels come from the paper's own simulator (Eq. 30); no code or data link or DOI, and no public channel dataset, is given.
notes: Included because a work that learns a physical-layer decision jointly with one above it passes above_phy: DDPG outputs the RIS phases (p. 6, 8) together with DDQN caching and offloading. Main metric is task delay, area 3 by function (RIS phase shifts). Fig. 3(c) DDPG comparison is on reward (negative delay); Figs. 4-8 compare delay. Table III (p. 9) lists no carrier frequency.
